title: Unit – 3 : Session – 2 : SLO – 1 | Creating Threads by Extending Thread
sections: Fill: In Java, a class can create a thread by extending the THREAD class.
T/F: The run() method contains the code that is executed by the thread. — TRUE
MCQ: Method used to start a Java thread → C) start()
Fill: A Java thread moves to the RUNNABLE state after calling the start() method.
T/F: The run() method is called directly to create and start a new thread. — FALSE (start() must be called; run() called directly executes on the current thread)
MCQ: Keyword used to define a subclass of Thread → B) extends
Fill: Calling start() on a Thread object internally calls the RUN() method.
T/F: A Java program can have multiple threads running at the same time. — TRUE
MCQ: Valid way to create a thread → A) Extend the Thread class
Fill: The Thread class is part of the java.lang PACKAGE.
